title: Mission-Critical Evals at Scale (Learnings from 100k medical decisions)
talk_summary: A medical-AI company describes building a real-time, reference-free eval layer (LLM-as-judge plus logic/confidence methods) that scores every production output before ground truth exists, then uses those confidence scores to prioritize which cases get scarce human review. This 'validating the validator' loop let them cover tens of thousands of cases with <10 clinical reviewers instead of hundreds, and eventually gate production outputs (auto-return vs. escalate to a stronger model/human).

takeaways.what_they_do: A reference-free eval assigns each output a confidence grade; low-confidence cases (combined with contextual risk factors) are prioritized for scarce human review instead of reviewing a fixed random percentage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can take our confidence grading ... combine those with contextual factors ... to dynamically prioritize the order for cases
takeaways.numbers: review tens of thousands of cases with a review team of less than 10 clinical experts; competitor hired 800+ nurses

takeaways.technique: Reference-free real-time eval on production traffic
takeaways.what_they_do: Run an LLM-as-judge (plus logic/confidence checks) on every live output before human ground truth exists, producing a real-time estimated accuracy across all cases, not just sampled ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: evaluating on live production data don't rely on offline evals identify problems immediately
takeaways.numbers: F1 near 96% in a recent study

takeaways.technique: Validate the validator (alignment between judge and humans)
takeaways.what_they_do: On the subset that does get human review, compare the reference-free eval's predicted correctness against the human verdict to compute alignment, then iterate the judge until it matches human reviewers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can compare those outputs based on that we can compute an alignment and see how well is our system doing

takeaways.what_they_do: Once the reference-free eval is trusted, it sits in the pipeline: high-confidence outputs go straight out, low-confidence ones escalate to a more expensive LLM pipeline or a human reviewer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: depending on what the reference free eval output is we can either give it back to the customer ... or we can decide to take a further action

takeaways.what_they_do: Built internal tooling that surfaces exactly the context a reviewer needs (input, output, source docs) on one screen with no scrolling, so reviewers process many cases quickly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of the context that our reviewer needs surfaced in an accessible way without any scrolling required

takeaways.what_they_do: When a reviewer marks an output wrong, capture a short critique of what's wrong, then generate a ground-truth description from critique+original answer to seed offline eval datasets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using that critique and the original answer we can then generate these ground truths and we can use those ground truths in offline evaluations
